references.text: God asks Abraham: "Is anything too hard for the Lord?" Then Sarah laughed at the thought of bearing a child in her old age. This confirms that nothing is impossible for God—the same principle Jesus states in [ref:1 Mos 18:14|Genesis 18:14].

Job acknowledges that no plan is too hard for God: "I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be thwarted." This affirms God's omnipotence as Jesus points to in [ref:Job 42:2|Job 42:2].
Jeremiah praises God and says: "Nothing is too hard for you." This is a direct parallel to Jesus' statement that what is impossible for humans is possible for God, see [ref:Jer 32:17|Jeremiah 32:17].

The Lord answers Jeremiah: "I am the Lord, the God of all flesh. Is anything too hard for me?" Yet another confirmation from Jeremiah that nothing is impossible for God, see [ref:Jer 32:27|Jeremiah 32:27].

Zechariah prophesies that even if something seems impossible in the eyes of the people, it is not impossible for the Lord of hosts. This text in [ref:Sak 8:6|Zechariah 8:6] shows the same principle as Jesus' words in Luke 18:27.
Matthew's parallel account where Jesus says: "For humans this is impossible, but for God all things are possible." This is the direct parallel to Luke 18:27, see [ref:Matt 19:26|Matthew 19:26].
Mark's parallel account where Jesus looks at the disciples and says: "For humans it is impossible, but not for God. For all things are possible with God." See [ref:Mark 10:27|Mark 10:27].

The angel Gabriel says to Mary: "For nothing is too hard for God." This statement in [ref:Luk 1:37|Luke 1:37] is an early confirmation in the Gospel of Luke of the same principle Jesus affirms in 18:27.

Paul describes Abraham's faith in God "who gives life to the dead and calls into being things that were not, as though they were." God's power surpasses human ability, as Jesus emphasizes in [ref:Rom 4:17|Romans 4:17].
Paul praises God "who is able to do far more abundantly than all that we ask or think." This underscores that God's power greatly exceeds human limitations, see [ref:Ef 3:20|Ephesians 3:20].
